title: Weekly Word: neep
description:
Meaning: turnip

Example: Mash the neeps gently before you serve.

Notes: Traditional Scottish vegetable word; used in ‘haggis, neeps & tatties’.

title: Weekly Word: stane
description:
Meaning: stone

Example: Throw the stane across the loch and watch the ripples.

Notes: Scots word for ‘stone’; shows how Scots uses its own terms even when English has cognates.

title: Weekly Word: mingin
description:
Meaning: foul smell / disgusting

Example: That’s a mingin bit of cheese — nae thanks.

Notes: Modern colloquial Scots word; gives strong character.

title: Weekly Word: wean
description:
Meaning: child

Example: The weans are all playing up in the yard.

Notes: Used particularly in West Central Scotland; variant of 'bairn'.

title: Weekly Word: farl
description:
Meaning: quarter piece of bread / flatbread

Example: Cut the oatcake into a farl and share it with tea.

Notes: Traditional Scottish baking term; the quarter of a round cake or oatcake.

title: Weekly Word: teuchter
description:
Meaning: rural Highlander (slang)

Example: He arrived in the city like a proper teuchter, gawky but full of stories.

Notes: Lowland Scots term, with cultural/historical resonance; best used with caution.

title: Weekly Word: wirry‑cow
description:
Meaning: bugbear, ghost

Example: As a bairn she’d say there was a wirry‑cow in the attic at night.

Notes: Scots compound word, vivid and folkloric in flavour.

title: Weekly Word: bairn
description:
Meaning: child

Example: Keep the bairn inside till the rain stops.

Notes: Common in eastern & northern Scotland; part of Scots vocabulary widely used.

title: Weekly Word: brae
description:
Meaning: hill or slope

Example: They climbed the steep brae to get a view over the loch.

Notes: Used in place‑names (The Braes o Balquhidder, Drumbrae) and in Scots dialect.
